newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain silent on "Operation Mengele" allegations.
newsitem.headline: Spain silent on "Operation Mengele" allegations.

text.p: Spain's defence ministry declined comment on Tuesday on a report that intelligence agents had kidnapped vagrants and used them as guinea pigs in tests on drugs for use in abductions of Basque rebels hiding in France.

The daily El Mundo, quoting military intelligence files, said the 1988 experiments, in which one beggar died, had been dubbed "Operation Mengele" within the service in reference to Nazi death camp doctor Josef Mengele.
A defence ministry spokeswoman told Reuters there would be no comment before the head of military intelligence could be reached for advice.

El Mundo, which revealed many of the scandals that led to the downfall in March of the 13-year-old Socialist government, said a beggar and two homeless drug addicts were abducted in July 1988 by members of a team of 53 intelligence agents driving stolen cars.

The aim was to test on them a drug designed to make it easier to abduct ETA (Basque Homeland and Freedom) separatists in hideaways in southern France and smuggle them into Spain, according to the documents quoted by El Mundo.
The drug was provided by a top Spanish cardiologist who was a close friend of then head of military intelligence General Emilio Alonso Manglano. El Mundo did not name the cardiologist.

A former Socialist interior minister and a top general in the paramilitary Civil Guard are on trial on charges of organising and running the death squads that waged a "dirty war" of kidnappings, torture and murder against ETA guerrillas, killing 27 people between 1983 and 1987.
